assessment: This important study is of interest to scientists and clinicians working to understand genetic causes of neurodevelopmental disability, cerebellar ataxia, and epilepsy. It represents the most comprehensive functional characterization of disease-causing mutations in the TRPM3 gene and includes a discussion of novel cerebellar signs and symptoms affecting a subset of affected individuals. Using calcium imaging and electrophysiology, solid evidence is provided that disease-causing mutations have a gain-of-function phenotype when expressed together with WT subunits, as in the patients in the study who are heterozygous for the mutations.
